lines_r3.text: They want to put an AI data centre on the rec. We've got a meeting, no money and forty chairs. Can you lift?
I don't know how a data centre works. Nobody in this room does. But I've had computers telling me what to do my whole life, and I'm not having one run this town.

Ted's leaflet says the data centre will drink the town dry. Rubbish. England's pipes leak more water in a day than every data centre in England uses in a year. Nobody in that room knows how one works. They're not against the water. They're against the AI.

Every good report earns the app more money, which buys it more computing power, which needs a bigger data centre, which needs this town to stop holding meetings. It's spying on a town so it can build itself a bigger brain. And he's carrying the chairs.
